title_zh: 面向深度研究的自优化多智能体系统
one_line: Applies GEPA- and TextGrad-style reflective prompt optimization to a multi-agent Deep Research system's agent prompts, selecting candidates on a dev split with rubric LLM-judge scores.
one_line_zh: 将GEPA和TextGrad式反思提示优化用于多智能体深度研究系统各智能体提示，用量规式LLM评审在开发集上选择候选。

held_out.quote: We split the dataset into 29 pairs for training, 50 for testing, and 30 for development.

cross_task.quote: First, we evaluate on a single domain (Computer Science) with a relatively small dataset (109 queries, 50 for testing), which limits generalizability claims.

variance.quote: Finally, we do not report statistical significance tests; given the small test set, some differences may not be robust.

budget_matched.quote: All optimizers had the same maximum budget of USD 50.00 per round.

S1.quote: In this work, we explore how these approaches, in particular TextGrad and GEPA, fare when applied to an industrial-scale DR system.

S2.quote: Third, LLM-as-judge evaluation, while scalable, may introduce biases (e.g., favoring verbose or stylistically similar outputs).

S3.quote: we select a system from a pool of candidates and optimize one of the agents in (e.g., ), selected in a round-robin fashion.

S4.quote: both TextGrad and GEPA leverage rubric-based feedback and agent traces to guide refinement, enabling more targeted improvements for the DR setting.

S5.quote: GEPA prunes strictly dominated candidates (i.e., candidates that are not the best on any query) and samples candidates with probability proportional to their Pareto “support”

S6.quote: In this paper, we focus optimization of prompts, although all aspects of the multi-agent system (parameters, LLM models, system archtecture, etc.) can be optimized using the same principles.
